clue.text: Find new life in jolly setting with an Army chap

indicators.note: in tells us the reworked letters sit inside the abbreviation for the jolly

parts.note: a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of the word life are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier discovers a new lease of life in cheerful surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' shuffles LIFE into IFLE, which goes 'in' RM; AN follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifleman is a soldier armed with a rifle, an infantry private in the British Army.

clue.text: He arranges shrouds with strict exactitude by word of mouth

indicators.note: by word of mouth says the clue's synonym is to be said out loud

parts.note: rigour is strict precision

explanation.surface: An undertaker who lays out shrouds with great precision, as heard in speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Shrouds are a ship's mast ropes, not burial cloths.
explanation.definitionFit: On a sailing ship the shrouds are part of the standing rope-work set up by this worker.

clue.text: Flamboyant man got-up to have a fling

definitions.text: man got-up to have a fling
definitions.meaning: describes a fellow dressed loudly for a night of fun

explanation.surface: A showy fellow dresses up for a romance.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means gaudy and showy, as a fellow dressed up for a spree would look.

clue.text: Valid result university gives to a student

parts.note: an effect is a result
taken as written
L, the learner plate, stands for a student

explanation.surface: An authentic exam outcome is awarded to an undergraduate.
explanation.definitionFit: Effectual means producing the intended effect, so legally binding or valid.

clue.text: Genuineness of a strange hit tune on London, say

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: strange says the letters of hit tune come out in an odd order

parts.note: London is an example of a city

explanation.surface: Questioning whether an odd pop song about London is the real thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Authenticity is the quality of being real rather than fake.

clue.text: Ludicrous descent from the Black Mountain

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
Mount Athos is the holy mountain in northern Greece

explanation.surface: A comical fall off a dark Welsh mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: The Black Mountain(s) suggests Wales, but Black gives B and Mountain is Athos in Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathos is the literary term for an absurd drop from the lofty to the trivial.

clue.text: Secret affair within a mile of us

parts.note: taken as written
our means belonging to us

explanation.surface: A clandestine romance happening very near to where we live.
explanation.definitionFit: French for love, used in English for an illicit love affair.

clue.text: "Barking dogs by —— pond" (Betjeman)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from John Betjeman's verse autobiography Summoned by Bells, naming a north London district

explanation.surface: A line of poetry with one word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Betjeman grew up near Hampstead Heath in north London; the ponds there are named after the neighbouring village.
explanation.definitionFit: The blank is filled by a north London suburb whose ponds lie on Hampstead Heath.

clue.text: Grating to mark the end of the way

parts.note: to scratch a surface is to mark it

indicators.note: the end of picks the final letter of the word way

explanation.surface: A grille placed to show where the road finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A scratchy sound or texture is harsh and rasping.

clue.text: "Mene, Mene, , Tekel, Upharsin," for example

parts.note: the words of the biblical writing on the wall at Belshazzar's feast, read as an example of words scrawled on a wall

explanation.surface: A quotation from the Book of Daniel offered as an example of something.
explanation.walkthrough: In Daniel 5 a hand writes these words on Belshazzar's palace wall; anything written on a wall without permission is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The writing on the wall is literally an inscription on a public wall, which is what street scrawls are.

clue.text: Rocks the boat

definitions.meaning: a geological name for a Jurassic rock series and for ironstone nodules
a two-masted Dutch fishing vessel of the North Sea

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a sandstone-and-ironstone rock bed and an old North Sea fishing smack.

clue.text: Rebuke for first tearing about

definitions.note: a noun here, matched by the gerund

indicators.note: about says the word for tearing goes round the word for first

parts.note: rending is tearing apart
prima is Italian for first, as in prima donna

explanation.surface: Telling someone off for being the first to rush around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts PRIMA inside RENDING, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprimanding is a scolding, the act of telling someone off.

clue.text: Code of conduct for some of the thick

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A set of rules for people who are not very bright.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a moral principle or set of principles governing behaviour.

clue.text: Ability to recognize vivid flower

parts.note: having an eye for something means being able to spot it
vivid colours are bright ones

explanation.surface: Being able to spot a brilliantly coloured bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphrasia, a small wild plant once used to treat eye complaints, bears that name.

clue.text: Confection to make a goat drink

parts.note: a goat butts, so it can be called a butter
Scotch is whisky

explanation.surface: A recipe for a sweet that involves giving a goat some whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: A goat is a 'butter' because it butts with its horns.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard brittle sweet made from sugar boiled with butter.

clue.text: May one not start to copy the French hymns?

parts.note: can't I means may I not, with one standing for I

indicators.note: start to picks the first letter of the word copy

parts.note: les is French for the

explanation.surface: A question about whether a person may begin to reproduce French songs of praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May one not?' is the question 'Can't I?', with I for 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Canticles are hymns or chants taken from the Bible, such as the Magnificat.

clue.text: Take-over notice on the right to buy or sell shares

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper

parts.words: the right to buy or sell shares
parts.note: an option is a contract giving that right at a set price

explanation.surface: A stock market announcement about a corporate takeover bid.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoption is taking something on as one's own, as of a child or a policy.

clue.text: Irregular partisan is hopeful

indicators.note: irregular says the letters of partisan are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A guerrilla fighter is optimistic.
explanation.walkthrough: An irregular partisan is a guerrilla, but 'Irregular' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirant is a hopeful, someone seeking a position or honour.

clue.text: Effect of fault in ship's weight

definitions.meaning: in geology a fault shifts rock strata relative to each other
a vessel's weight equals that of the water it pushes aside

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the movement of rock along a geological fault and the water a floating vessel shifts, equal to its mass.

clue.text: Dismiss the form

definitions.meaning: in some British public schools a form, or class, is named this

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to take away or oust, and in some British schools it names an intermediate class.

clue.text: Northern town with a green

parts.note: a Cumbrian market town famous for a green woollen cloth named after it

explanation.walkthrough: Kendal green was a coarse green cloth worn by woodsmen, mentioned by Falstaff in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in Cumbria in north-west England gave its name to a green cloth.

clue.text: American university print, once in pieces

indicators.note: in pieces says the letters of print and once are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A printed old document at a US college has fallen apart.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ivy League institution in New Jersey.

clue.text: Make slow progress (but not as a swimmer).

definitions.text: Make slow progress (but not as a swimmer).

parts.words: Make slow progress (but not as a swimmer).
parts.note: the verb for inching along, with a nod to the fastest swimming stroke, which shares its name

explanation.surface: Moving slowly, though not in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the word for slow progress also names the fastest swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep along on hands and knees or in heavy traffic.

clue.text: One Frenchman's girl

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
René is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: The young woman belonging to a single French man.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so a crossword stand-in for any girl.

clue.text: I have it — the first year of the Muslim prophet

parts.note: taken as written
it is old slang for sex appeal, SA
I is the Roman numeral one, the first
AH, anno Hegirae, dates years in the Islamic calendar

explanation.surface: A claim to have found the first year of the Islamic calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muslim prophet' reads as one phrase, but 'the Muslim' ends the AH piece and 'prophet' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament book is named after the Hebrew seer it records.

clue.text: Miss Rhymer had hers when young

parts.note: a miss is a young unmarried woman
Thomas Hood was a Victorian comic poet, a writer of rhymes

explanation.surface: A Miss Rhymer had her own childhood once.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hood (1799-1845) wrote humorous verse such as 'Faithless Nelly Gray'.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's youth is the time before adulthood, her early years as a young female.

clue.text: Cause provocation in the plant

definitions.meaning: a stinging weed of the genus Urtica

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to irk, and as a noun it names a stinging weed.

clue.text: Kind of paint colour in China

definitions.meaning: a pale off-white shade and a low-sheen paint finish

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a pale off-white shade with a soft sheen and very thin, fragile porcelain.
